codeReview.summary: The implementation correctly updates the CLI event-kind checks to handle both new and legacy StreamEventKind values. The 'text'/'assistant_token', 'reasoning'/'reasoning_step', and 'done'/'final' mappings are accurate and match what the streaming layer actually emits. The 'cancelled' legacy block is preserved correctly because forced_routing.py still emits kind='cancelled' directly. The cast(Any, ...) removal and its unused import cleanup are correct — build_chat_agent already has return type Any, making the cast redundant. All four validators (format, lint, typecheck, test) passed.

issues.description: Pre-existing issue (not introduced by this commit): the live-event-queue filter at line 482 uses a hardcoded set {"final", "cancelled", "error"} instead of the module-level TERMINAL_STREAM_EVENT_KINDS frozenset, which also includes 'done'. This means 'done' terminal events are not filtered from the live event callback queue. This discrepancy predates this feature and is out of scope here but worth tracking.

sharedStateObservations.observation: TERMINAL_STREAM_EVENT_KINDS (streaming.py:54) is defined as a frozenset that includes 'done', but the live-event-queue filter function (_setup_live_event_queue, line 482) uses a hardcoded set that omits 'done'. This is a pre-existing inconsistency in the streaming layer — the module constant is not reused where it should be. Worth documenting in AGENTS.md or fixing in a follow-up.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/fleet_rlm/runtime/execution/streaming.py:54 defines TERMINAL_STREAM_EVENT_KINDS = frozenset({"done", "final", "cancelled", "error"}); line 482 uses if event.kind in {"final", "cancelled", "error"}: — missing 'done'

summary: Pass. Both changes are correct and complete: (1) CLI chat.py now handles text/reasoning/done alongside the legacy assistant_token/reasoning_step/final/cancelled kinds, with the cancelled-via-done payload path also handled; (2) cast(Any, ...) removed from chat_runtime.py with the unused cast import cleaned up. Validators all green. One pre-existing non-blocking discrepancy noted in streaming.py (TERMINAL_STREAM_EVENT_KINDS not reused in live-event filter) — not introduced by this feature.
